prompt: What does a conditional forwarder configure?
options: A rule sending queries for a specified DNS namespace to selected DNS servers
A complete read-only copy of every record in that namespace
An IP address pool for DHCP clients
An Active Directory trust between two domains
en: The condition is the queried DNS namespace; matching questions go to configured DNS destinations.
ru: Condition queried DNS namespace hai; matching sawal configured DNS destinations ko jate hain.

prompt: What does a conditional-forwarder rule store for its basic operation?
options: The domain to match and target DNS server addresses
Every host A and PTR record in the target zone
Client passwords and Kerberos tickets
The target network’s complete switch configuration
en: The rule identifies where to ask, not a transferred inventory of host records.
ru: Rule batata hai kahan poochna hai; host records ki transferred inventory nahin.

prompt: How does a conditional forwarder differ from a standard secondary zone?
options: It forwards matching questions rather than holding a full authoritative zone copy
It always stores more zone records than a secondary
It is a writable primary copy under another name
It replaces the client’s network adapter
en: A secondary replicates full zone data; a conditional rule routes queries.
ru: Secondary full zone data replicate karta hai; conditional rule queries bhejta hai.

prompt: Which comparison with a stub zone is accurate?
options: A stub maintains authority metadata; a conditional forwarder uses configured query destinations
Both necessarily contain every ordinary host record
A stub sets the default gateway; forwarding creates PTRs
A conditional forwarder always discovers every changed authority automatically
en: The mechanisms differ: authority discovery versus a configured namespace-to-server rule.
ru: Mechanisms alag: authority discovery aur configured namespace-to-server rule.

prompt: Does creating a conditional forwarder make the local server authoritative for the destination domain?
options: No; configuring a query destination does not confer zone authority
Yes; all matching domain records become writable locally
Yes; authority transfers as soon as the dialog is saved
Only if the target address is a private IPv4 address
en: Forwarding configuration alone does not establish authoritative zone ownership.
ru: Sirf forwarding configuration authoritative zone ownership establish nahin karti.

prompt: Which DNS Manager area creates a domain-specific forwarding rule?
options: Conditional Forwarders node
Reverse Lookup Zones only
The client’s hosts file editor
The Network Adapter IPv4 gateway field
en: Conditional Forwarders is distinct from the server-wide general Forwarders settings.
ru: Conditional Forwarders node server-wide general Forwarders settings se alag hai.

prompt: What is the role of an ordinary server-level forwarder?
options: Handle eligible unresolved queries through a general forwarding path
Maintain the writable source for every remote zone
Provide the client’s default IP route
Create every reverse record automatically
en: General forwarding and namespace-specific forwarding have different scope.
ru: General aur namespace-specific forwarding ka scope alag hai.

prompt: What remains necessary when the target DNS server is on another subnet?
options: Working network routing and permitted DNS traffic
Only a matching wallpaper on both machines
Only a CNAME pointing to the subnet mask
No network path because forwarding creates one
en: A DNS rule does not create an IP route, tunnel or firewall exception.
ru: DNS rule IP route, tunnel ya firewall exception create nahin karta.

prompt: Is zone-transfer permission required merely to forward a DNS query?
options: No; query forwarding and zone transfer are different operations
Yes; every query must download the full zone
Yes; otherwise the client must become a secondary
Only when the queried name contains a final dot
en: Queries ask for answers; zone transfer replicates zone data.
ru: Query answer poochti hai; zone transfer zone data replicate karta hai.

prompt: Which transport access should be considered for normal DNS operation?
options: Both UDP and TCP port 53 as appropriate
Only TCP port 3389
Only UDP port 67
Only HTTPS port 443 without a DNS service
en: DNS commonly uses UDP and also needs TCP for appropriate responses and operations.
ru: DNS aam tor par UDP use karta aur munasib responses/operations ke liye TCP bhi chahiye.

prompt: What was the saved classroom conditional-forwarder destination for KRNC.org?
en: The recorded KRNC.org rule on DNS01 points to 172.16.0.18.
ru: DNS01 ka recorded KRNC.org rule 172.16.0.18 ko point karta hai.

prompt: On which classroom server was the KRNC.org rule saved?
options: A client identified only by its subnet mask
en: DNS01 is the documented rule’s local forwarding server.
ru: Documented rule ka local forwarding server DNS01 hai.

prompt: A rule matches KRNC.org. Which illustrative name falls within that namespace?
options: app.krnc.org.
app.vcplab.com.
krnc.org.example.
app.otherorg.example.
en: The name app.krnc.org is under KRNC.org; it is illustrative, not a verified existing record.
ru: app.krnc.org, KRNC.org ke andar hai; yeh misaal hai, verified existing record nahin.

prompt: DNS01 has the local authoritative VCPLAB.Com zone and a KRNC.org forwarder. What normally answers a known local dns02.vcplab.com record?
options: DNS01’s local authoritative zone data
The KRNC.org rule solely because it was added last
The target subnet’s default gateway as a DNS record
The conditional rule automatically removes the local zone
en: The local hosted zone covers the queried name; the unrelated KRNC.org rule is not its route.
ru: Local hosted zone queried naam cover karti hai; unrelated KRNC.org rule us ka route nahin.

prompt: The input 172.16.018 causes an entry error. Which correction matches the recorded intended target?
en: The documented target is the four-octet IPv4 address 172.16.0.18.
ru: Documented target chaar-octet IPv4 address 172.16.0.18 hai.

prompt: The rule is saved and its target address is displayed. Which statement matches the available classroom evidence?
options: Configuration was saved; successful KRNC.org resolution was not demonstrated
Every KRNC.org record is now verified
Routing to the target is automatically proven
A trust-anchor validation test has completed
en: A saved configuration is not an end-to-end resolution test.
ru: Saved configuration end-to-end resolution test nahin.

prompt: The host-only lab is 192.168.0.0/24 with no configured gateway. The rule points to 172.16.0.18. What needs checking?
options: Whether any valid network path to that other subnet exists
Whether saving the DNS rule created a router automatically
Whether all machines must rename themselves KRNC
Whether the local subnet mask is a DNS server address
en: Host-only membership alone does not provide routing to another private subnet.
ru: Host-only membership akeli doosri private subnet tak routing nahin deti.

prompt: A real known-host.krnc.org record has been confirmed by the instructor. Which comparison is most useful?
options: Query it directly at 172.16.0.18, then through DNS01 at .121
Query an unrelated Google name twice
Ping DNS02 and assume the forwarding path works
Check only that the local CNAME exists
en: The direct-versus-forwarded comparison separates target service/data from the forwarding path.
ru: Direct aur forwarded comparison target service/data ko forwarding path se alag karta hai.

prompt: A successful query through DNS01 might have used cached data. What additional evidence helps establish forwarding occurred?
options: Relevant query logs or a packet capture of the DNS01-to-target exchange
Only the presence of the rule in the console
Only the client’s DNS suffix
Only the current desktop hostname
en: A returned answer alone does not establish the precise upstream packet path.
ru: Returned answer akela exact upstream packet path establish nahin karta.

prompt: The target address changes. What must be reviewed for a manually configured conditional forwarder?
options: Its configured target list and connectivity to the new destination
Only the client’s desktop theme
Only the target zone’s MX record
Nothing, because all configured addresses update automatically
en: A manually configured destination needs lifecycle management when addresses change.
ru: Manually configured destination ka address badlay to uski management chahiye.

prompt: Direct queries to the target DNS time out. What should be investigated before blaming DNS01’s rule?
options: Target service, route, DNS access controls and permitted traffic
Only DNS01’s reverse-zone capitalization
Only the order of unrelated CNAME records
Delete the local primary zone immediately
en: Failure directly at the destination suggests a target or path issue to investigate.
ru: Destination ko direct query fail ho to target ya path investigate karna chahiye.

prompt: The target answers directly, but the same name fails through DNS01. What is a focused next check?
options: The exact namespace rule, target list and DNS01’s own path/policy
Assume the target is down despite the direct answer
Rename the test client to match the remote domain
Promote DNS02 just to change the destination rule
en: The forwarding server can have different reachability and policy from the testing client.
ru: Forwarding server ki reachability aur policy testing client se mukhtalif ho sakti hai.

prompt: The target returns a valid NXDOMAIN for a misspelled name. What expectation is wrong?
options: The resolver must keep trying other paths until it finds an address
The query spelling should be checked
The target returned a negative DNS response
The name may be absent from the target namespace
en: A valid negative reply is not the same as silence and does not normally trigger an answer hunt.
ru: Valid negative reply silence nahin; aam tor par pasand ka answer dhoondne ka trigger nahin.

prompt: DNS-A forwards the same namespace to DNS-B, while DNS-B forwards it back to DNS-A without either resolving it. What is the risk?
options: A forwarding loop leading to failed or delayed resolution
Automatic creation of authoritative records
Automatic replication of a complete zone
Guaranteed successful load balancing
en: Circular rules can send unresolved work back and forth rather than to a source of answers.
ru: Circular rules unresolved sawal ko answers ke source ke bajaye wapas bhej sakti hain.

prompt: A target stops responding. Is fallback to another resolution path guaranteed?
options: No; it depends on recursion/fallback settings, timeouts and usable connectivity
Yes; every query always reaches public root servers
Yes; a conditional rule becomes a secondary automatically
No; every timeout permanently deletes the forwarding rule
en: Fallback is conditional, not proof that another reachable resolution path exists.
ru: Fallback conditional hai; doosra reachable resolution path honay ka proof nahin.
